the gender identity better explains the individual differences in the episodic autobiographical memories, while the sex better explains the individual difference in the semantic autobiographical memories and conceptual self.
gender identity is a better predictor of inter individual differences in EAM than sex, but the effects are not limited to EAM only.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the feminine gender identity is associated with more emotional aspects in AM, while the masculine gender identity is associated only with the emotional aspects of episodic AM.
gender identity, more than sex, explains individual differences in the way we remember and think about our personal past and future.
gender identity better explains individual differences in emotional aspects of AM and future orientation, while sex is associated with limited effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gender identity is an important factor in the study of autobiographical and self knowledge.
gender identity, rather than sex, should be considered in research on AM and self-knowledge.
, in the future, researchers and clinicians should take into consideration gender identity rather than sex when studying individual differences in AM.
